CPS I/O Unix Domain Sockets

Provides Unix domain socket client (UnixStream) and server (UnixListener) for local IPC, integrated with the CPS event loop.

Imports

../runtime, ../eventloop, ../private/platform, streams

Types

UnixListener = ref object
  fd*: SocketHandle
  path*: string
  closed*: bool
UnixStream = ref object of AsyncStream
  fd*: SocketHandle

Connect to a Unix domain socket at path asynchronously. Returns a UnixStream. 
proc unixListen(path: string; backlog: int = 128): UnixListener {.
    ...raises: [AsyncIoError, OSError], tags: [ReadIOEffect], forbids: [].}
Create a Unix domain socket listener. Binds to the given path and starts listening. This is a synchronous operation -- the socket is ready for accept() calls. If the socket file already exists it will be unlinked first. 
proc unixSocketIsReachable(path: string): bool {....raises: [], tags: [],
    forbids: [].}
Return true only when a process is actively accepting connections at path. A Unix socket directory entry can outlive its owner, so checking the filesystem alone is not enough for daemon discovery.
